ideas.name: TikTok POV: interrogating the friend who says he's 'up overall'
ideas.oneLiner: A two-person interrogation skit where the friend who's always up gets asked one follow-up question too many.
ideas.headline: On-screen text: 'asking my friend who's always up some follow-up questions'. Friend, first line, flat: 'I'm up overall.'
ideas.backlash: Nobody much. Maybe the friends who got tagged.
ideas.mechanism:
Two people at a kitchen table, one desk lamp pointed at the friend like an interrogation room. Low suspense sound from the trending list, quiet under the dialogue.
Beat 1 (0-2s): Friend: 'I'm up overall.'
Beat 2: Me: 'Since when.' Friend: 'Since a date I've chosen.'
Beat 3: Me: 'What about March.' Friend: 'March isn't in the sample.'
Beat 4: Me: 'Show me.' Friend slides his phone across the table, face down. He doesn't flip it.
Beat 5: Me: 'That's the back of your phone.' Friend, not blinking: 'That's the overall.'
Hard cut to black. Small cashy watermark bottom corner.
Caption: 'everyone has one. 18+'
ideas.borrowedAttention: The 'friend who's always up' in-joke and the interrogation-room skit format.
ideas.effort: 2 people, phone on a tripod, one lamp, CapCut for captions. 1 hour.

consequences: Fake chat overlay should use invented usernames and a generic stream layout, not a real streamer's channel name or face. That avoids any implied endorsement problem.

The bit is a gambling-stream in-joke with no product, offer or link, so platform risk is low. TikTok can still limit reach on a casino-branded account. Cashy's watermark plus the 18+ caption keeps it clearly labelled rather than disguised.

Some viewers may read the obsessive chatter as a nod to gambling harm. It works as a joke about the chatter's faith in the streamer, not a push to play. Keep it there and don't add any CTA or bonus reference that turns his persistence into encouragement.
The actor should clearly look over 25 to stay inside the brand's minor-appeal rule. Avoid a teen-bedroom set (posters, school items).

ideas.name: Series: 9am me investigating what 3am me did
ideas.oneLiner: A recurring true-crime parody where your morning self investigates the damage your 3am self did.
ideas.headline: On-screen text: '9am me investigating what 3am me did, episode 1'. A torch clicks on.
ideas.mechanism:
One person plays both versions of themselves.
Episode 1, 'the 3am transaction':
Beat 1: 9am me in a dressing gown with a mug and a notepad. True-crime voiceover, low and serious: 'The wallet was discovered at 9:02am.'
Beat 2: Shines a phone torch onto another phone like it's evidence. VO: 'Last known activity: 3:14am. The note just says "trust".'
Beat 3: Cut to 3am me. Hood up, screen brightness at 1%, whispering: 'trust.'
Beat 4: Back to 9am me, who writes 'TRUST' on the notepad, circles it twice and stares into the camera.
End card in the default font: 'case remains open'. Corner watermark: cashy. Caption: '18+'.
Future episodes: the 3am leveraged long, the 3am 'u up' text, the 3am 40-nugget order, the 3am coin named after a flying car, the 3am Amazon cart.
ideas.borrowedAttention: True-crime TikTok narration and the 'me at 3am vs me in the morning' genre. Trenchers will get the flying-car coin episode.
ideas.effort: 1 person, phone, dressing gown, notepad, CapCut voice filter. 1 hour per episode, batch 6 in a day.
ideas.shelfLife: Weeks to months as a series
ideas.platform: TikTok and Reels, 3 episodes a week

tests.note: '9am me investigating what 3am me did, episode 1' plus the torch click. Numbered, so it promises more.

tests.note: An endless list of 3am cases, comment-driven, numbered episodes. No crypto casino has a recurring self-detective character.

reasons: The 3am-vs-daytime-me idea is familiar, but the true-crime case-file frame gives it a fixed, bingeable format.
Non-gambling episodes push reach well past the niche while the account stays Cashy's.
Episode 1's 'trust' punchline is a bit soft. Lead with the 40-nugget or 'u up' case and keep 'trust' for later.

priorArt.summary: Web check skipped on this test run.

consequences: No red line is breached. It is a relatable self-parody about late-night impulse decisions. It does not show a deposit flow, a casino UI or a sign-up push, so no market-specific issue comes up from the content itself. If it gets boosted or targeted, legal should check that paid distribution excludes markets where Cashy doesn't take players (for example the US, the UK if unlicensed, Australia).

Responsible gambling angle: the joke is built on 3am compulsive behaviour (impulse wallet activity, leveraged longs). It is played as self-aware degen humour, not as encouragement, so it is fine. Keep it that way. No episode should show a gambling loss as something to chase or fix, and none should frame money trouble being solved by a win. A critic could still read 'case remains open' plus a casino watermark as making light of late-night problem gambling. Expect some RG-advocate quote-tweets.
Minor appeal: the dressing gown, mug and home setting are neutral. Cast talent who clearly reads 25+, and avoid anything that looks like a bedroom or school setting for the hooded 3am character.

The '3am coin named after a flying car' episode nods to the live $FTR / flying Tesla Roadster memecoin. Only mock the behaviour of aping in. Don't name or show a real token contract in a way that reads as a shill or as accusing anyone of a rug, or it could drift toward defamation of the token's creators.
The '3am u up text' and '40-nugget order' episodes are harmless. Keep any on-screen phone screens fictional so no real person's number or messages show up.

Platform risk is low. A casino watermark on TikTok/Reels can still trigger gambling-content review on some accounts, and the 18+ caption helps. The format isn't disguised promotion, so the account-loss risk is minimal as long as no episode slips in a casino screen or bonus.

consequences: A man kneeling outside a locked bathroom door with a crisis negotiator after a 50x leverage loss can read as a suicide or self-harm crisis scene. Crypto and gambling losses have real cases like that, so expect some quote-tweets calling it tasteless. Keep it absurd (clipboard, cheap windbreaker, walkie-talkie, mum) and never show or hint at self-harm. Don't post it next to any news of a real trader or gambler death.

Self-aware irony: a casino account posting a bit where the hero talks people out of 'one more bonus buy' will get 'you of all people' replies. That's fine and on-voice, but community managers should have a deadpan reply ready, not a defensive one.

Responsible-gambling critics may read the 'one more bonus buy' and 7-leg parlay episodes either as mocking intervention or as normalising it. Keep the negotiator competent and the friend the joke, never the person trying to stop.

The episode about the flying Tesla coin names a live memecoin ($FTR or the Chinese-ticker version). Mocking it is fine. Don't show a ticker or contract address in a way that reads as a shill or pump, and don't call it a scam as fact.

Platform risk is low. It's a skit with an 18+ caption and no gambling promotion. TikTok may still limit reach for gambling-adjacent accounts, and the bathroom hostage framing could trip violence or crisis classifiers. Avoid real guns or police props.

Market: the content is watchable anywhere and pushes no sign-ups, so there's no market-specific breach. If it's ever paired with a CTA or link in bio to deposits, legal should check UK/AU/US-state exposure, since 'bonus buy' references are sensitive in the UK, where bonus buys are banned under UKGC rules.
Casting: the negotiator and 'Mike' must clearly look over 25 to stay clear of the minors rule.

memories.text: Simple content beats big campaigns. Nobody is doing big wild stunts: no IRL stunts, sponsorships, purchases, product drops or 'campaigns'. Every idea is a post, video, slideshow, meme, reply, recurring bit or tiny vibe-coded build that one or two people can make this week, that gets views on its own and fits how the new-gen audience is funny (deadpan, relatable, self-aware, absurd). If it sounds like AI or an agency wrote it, or it's cheesy or gimmicky, it's dead.

Get Cashy in front of as many people as possible with things that are good on their own and subtly carry Cashy's name (posting account, watermark, logo in the corner). Never an idea that tells people why Cashy is great.
